Sara —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I'm kicking off the renewal + expansion coordination for BrightLoop (BL-4392). High-level goals we heard: extend term to cover two new product modules, add a predictable burst capacity pool for peak traffic, and keep the per-token economics within the committed threshold.

Attached is a draft mutual action plan (BL_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v0.9.docx) with milestones and a first-pass timeline. My asks to start:
- Can you confirm the exec & procurement stakeholders we should include?
- Are there any internal blackout dates for an October QBR week?
- Do you have a preferred date window for a kickoff QBR (30–60 min)?

Proposed next steps (short):
1) You share stakeholder list + procurement contact (if not already on thread)
2) We share capacity workbook and prelim pricing options (attached from our side)
3) Schedule a 30-min QBR to align on roadmap, SOW, and timeline

I’ll loop in Laura (CS lead) and Karthik (solutions/infra) who will own capacity sizing and implementation timeline.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin

Subject: Re: BrightLoop upgrade path: multiproduct renewal kickoff

Sara + Tom —

Thanks — looping in Laura (CS) and Karthik (Solutions) to drive sizing and term options. I’ve attached the capacity workbook (BrightLoop_capacity_workbook.xlsx) with two scenarios:

Scenario A — Staggered commit (recommended): 24-month term, staircase commit with a 30% uplift in month 7 to accommodate the second module; includes a reserved burst pool that can be consumed at a lower incremental cost.
Scenario B — Pilot + convert: 3-month pilot for module B (lower commit) then convert to a 12–18 month commit if KPIs met.

Laura/Karthik: can you review the workbook and confirm the assumptions below are aligned with BrightLoop’s traffic profile? If yes, we’ll convert to a formal SOW and run the legal/commercial thread:
- baseline tokens/day: 25M (module A live), projected tokens/day after both modules: 70–85M
- typical request concurrency: 120–180 requests/sec, peak bursts up to 600 concurrent requests for short windows
- target p99 latency for the critical endpoints: <120ms

Proposed QBR: Oct 5, 11am PT (30 min) — hold as tentative until exec confirms. If Oct 4 week is preferable, we can move.

Attachments: BrightLoop_capacity_workbook.xlsx

Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLoop upgrade path: multiproduct renewal kickoff

Quick technical read —

Thanks for the workbook. High level: we can support the projected baseline and the burst profile with the following notes:
- We recommend a dedicated GPU pool for the two new modules with autoscale headroom sized to support short bursts to ~600 concurrent inference sessions. That keeps latency predictable and reduces cross-tenant noise.
- For cost control, enable prefix/KV caching for shared prompts and set an aggressive batching policy for non-critical endpoints.
- Implementation estimate: 4–6 weeks from PO acceptance for the pool + rollout, including config, smoke tests, and a canary rollout.

Needed from BrightLoop for firm sizing: hourly traffic histogram for 30 days (UTC), and 5 sample input payloads for each module to validate model sequence length distributions.

I’ll draft a short implementation runbook once I have the histogram.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
